title: How It Works
metaTitle: How It Works - Selling Your Royalty Interest
metaDescription: The step-by-step process for selling an oil and gas royalty or mineral interest, from first contact to funds at closing, no broker involved.
heroLead: Six steps, no broker in the middle, and nothing that requires you to be an expert before you start.
intro: Owners often expect this to be complicated because the underlying asset is unfamiliar. The process itself isn't - it's closer to selling a piece of property than owners expect, and most of it is paperwork we handle, not you.
Here's the sequence from first contact to funds landing in your account.

sections.heading: Start with whatever paperwork you have
paragraphs: Statements, a deed, a division order, or just a county and legal description if that's all you've got. Incomplete paperwork isn't a barrier to starting - it just means we may need to pull some county records ourselves to fill gaps before we can put a full picture together. Some owners begin with a full file; others begin with a family story and a rough sense of where the minerals sit, and both are workable starting points.

sections.heading: We evaluate the actual interest, not a county average
paragraphs: We review your decimal interest, recent production and decline behavior where statements exist, and any nearby drilling or permit activity. For non-producing minerals, we look at leasing activity and offset wells in the area instead, since there's no check history to model from. This is the step where our background on the operating side actually shows up - reading a decline curve and a deduction line the way an engineer reads them, not the way a form letter summarizes them.

sections.heading: A written offer, with reasoning attached
paragraphs: Typically within a few business days once we have enough to work with. The offer explains what it's based on - we don't send a bare number and expect you to trust it on faith. There's no cost and no obligation attached to receiving it.

sections.heading: Take your time deciding
paragraphs: Take the time you need. Compare it against another offer if you want to. Ask us anything about how we arrived at the number - a legitimate offer holds up to questions. There's no expiration pressure attached to a fair one.

sections.heading: Title work and the purchase agreement
paragraphs: If you accept, we prepare a purchase and sale agreement stating exactly what's being conveyed and the price, and begin confirming title. This is the step most likely to surface an inherited-interest issue - an unresolved heirship or missing probate - and we'll walk you through what's needed to clear it if it comes up.

sections.heading: Signing, recording, and funds at closing
paragraphs: Once title is clear, you sign the mineral deed, we record it at the county, and funds are disbursed by wire or check depending on your preference. We also handle notifying the operator's division order department so future royalty routes correctly, if any is still owed to you between now and the effective date.

sections.heading: After closing
paragraphs: Once funds are disbursed and the deed is recorded, our involvement in that interest is done, and the closing documents you receive are what you'll hand to your CPA at tax time. If a royalty check for prior production still arrives in the mail after closing, hold onto it and check the effective date in your purchase agreement - it may still be yours depending on the timing.

If you sold a fractional interest and kept the rest, your existing checks continue as before on the portion you retained, unaffected by the sale beyond the reduced decimal reflecting what you no longer own.

faqs.question: How long does the whole process take?
faqs.answer: It depends mostly on title condition. A clean title with straightforward ownership can close in a matter of weeks; interests requiring heirship documentation or probate take longer because that has to clear first.

faqs.question: Do you have to accept the first offer?
faqs.answer: No. There's no obligation at any point until you sign a purchase agreement, and you're free to walk away, negotiate, or simply take time to decide.

faqs.question: What if a title issue comes up during the process?
faqs.answer: It's common with older inherited interests and rarely stops a sale - it just adds a documentation step, usually an affidavit of heirship or a short probate process, which we'll explain clearly if it applies to your file.

faqs.question: Who pays for closing costs and title work?
faqs.answer: Typically we do, as part of the transaction. Terms are spelled out in the purchase agreement before you sign, so confirm this in writing rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Can you back out after receiving an offer?
faqs.answer: Yes, up until you sign a purchase agreement, there's no obligation to proceed. Even after signing, most agreements include reasonable contingencies tied to clean title - ask directly what flexibility your specific agreement includes.

faqs.question: Does the process differ for non-producing minerals?
faqs.answer: The overall sequence is the same, but the evaluation step relies on nearby activity and leasing data instead of statement history, since there's no production to model directly.

faqs.question: What if you own interests in more than one county?
faqs.answer: Send details on all of them together. We can evaluate multiple tracts as one file, which is often simpler for you than handling each as a separate transaction.
